text.p: Following are some of the major events to have occurred on December 10 in history.
1508 - The League of Cambrai was formed by Pope Julius II, Holy Roman Emperor Maximilian I, Louis XII of France and Ferdinand II of Aragon, to attack Venice.
1520 - Martin Luther publicy burned the papal bull excommunicating him.
1817 - Mississippi became the 20th of the United States.
1819 - Felice Orsini, Italian nationalist revolutionary, born; he tried to assassinate Napoleon III in the belief that it would cause a revolution in France which would spread to Italy.
1845 - The first pneumatic tyres were patented by British civil engineer Robert Thompson.
1851 - American librarian Melvil Dewey, who devised the system of classification for library cataloguing,s born.
1865 - Leopold I, the first king of the Belgians and highly influential in European diplomacy, died.
1868 - The world's first traffic lights, built off London's Parliament Square, began operation.
1891 - 1st Earl Alexander of Tunis, British commander in Burma, North Africa and Mediterranean during World War Two, born.

1896 - Swedish industrialist Alfred Nobel died; he made much of his fortune from his invention of dynamite and used it to found the Nobel prizes, the first of which were handed out on this day in 1901.
1898 - The Treaty of Paris was signed, ending the Spanish-American War. The independence of Cuba was agreed and Guam, Puerto Rico and the Philippines were ceded to the U.S.
1902 - The original Aswan Dam, built by the British to control the Nile flood, was completed.
1914 - American actress Dorothy Lamour was born; best remembered for appearances in the "Road" films with Bob Hope and Bing Crosby.
1924 - Malcolm Manley, Jamaican prime minister from 1972-80 and 1989-92, born.
1931 - Alasara Zamora was chosen as Spain's first constitutionally-elected president.
1941 - Japanese planes sank the British battleships "Repulse" and "Prince of Wales" in the South China Sea, killing nearly 800.
1963 - Zanzibar, a British protectorate since 1890, became an independent state within the Commonwealth.
1967 - Otis Redding, one of the most influential soul singers of the 1960s, was killed in a plane crash in Winconsin.
1979 - The parliament of Zimbabwe-Rhodesia met for the last time to vote itself out of existence.
1982 - The U.N. Convention on the Law of the Sea was signed by 119 countries - but not Britain or the United States.
1982 - Two Soviet cosmonauts returned to Earth after spending a record 211 days in space aboard Salyut 7.
1983 - Raul Alfonsin was inaugurated as Argentina's civilian president after eight years of military rule.
1987 - Jascha Heifetz, world famous violinist noted for his conscientious musical interpretation and technical proficiency, died.
1989 - Czechoslovakia's first government without a Communist majority since 1948 assumed power and President Gustav Husak resigned.
1990 - Armand Hammer, chairman of Occidental Petroleum, died at the age of 92.
1990 - Toyehiro Akiyama, the first journalist and Japanese national to go into space, returned to Earth after an eight-day mission.
1993 - Three Britons imprisoned in Iraq were freed after former British prime minister Sir Edward Heath flew to Baghdad to appeal for their release.
1995 - Israeli soldiers quit the West Bank town of Tulkarm and a first contingent of PLO police moved in to Hebron as part of a handover to Palestinian rule.
1995 - NASA scientists received the first data from the space probe Galileo -- a message beamed over 2.3 billion miles (3.7 billion km).
